ENS does commit-reveal to prevent front running and it works really well. Yes of course. Fbs can even run an auction (if they're fast enough), but I've done the analysis. What is the elevator pitch for why you believe that having a smaller pool of things to choose from will reduce MEV? There are some extremely advanced MEV strategies that involve doing whole block organization that may work less, but I don't think anyone is actually doing this. I *think* it would require a full AI to. Block reorgs are a different problem. Im solving for centralization of block content. This is different than current frontrun/backrun/sandwich things that generally look at one or two transactions to extract value from at a time. A sandwich happening 2 minutes after a transaction was sent usually just means there was minimal value to extract or there was a long block. not theoretic ... CEX arbs already happening. And if we're forward looking to eth2 .. then the CEXes might directly own the very validators whose block txs theyre arbing against More frequent blocks wouldn't have prevented that sandwich if it was worth sandwiching. yup but thats just sandwich Yes they would because the victim tx only became value after 2 mins, otherwise by definition it would have been sandwiched before 1 second transaction batches either won't work or will result in *massive* churn because network propagation time is significantly longer than 1 second. The victim transaction still would have sat in the pending pool for 2 minutes just the same. Yeah I said 1 to 3 secs Even 3 seconds is likely too fast for network propogation. No, its execution order would be guaranteed after 3 secs Things are probably faster these days, but it used to be that network propagation was around 6 seconds. I think its a lot faster now, like a couple of 100ms The victim transaction sat in the pending pool for 2 minutes because its gas price was too low to be included. No miner was willing to include that transaction over any other transaction. It definitely is not! It takes something like 250ms just to direct-connect round trip via neutrino from one side of the planet to the other. 😄 It is literally physically impossible to have global transaction propagation be faster than the speed of light around the planet. 😄 Well, given our current understanding of physics. Sure that's probably a bit low, but not the point, I was talking about 3 secs Maybe something with entangled quantum particles we can do better one day. 😉 Reality is also way more complicated then theory. For a transaction or block to propogate, it has to hope between nodes in a global peer to peer network and each node has to do a non-trivial amount of validation of the block before propogating. There we have it, users now have to wait until their txs become exploitable to get included yup you need to shrink the validator set. which is fine for L2 On a "normal" computer I think block validation takes on the order of hundreds of milliseconds, which means each hop in the network takes network travel time (which is non zero) and validation time (which is non zero). If you assume 10 hops between any two points in the network, this whole process takes a while. If you are talking about having *all* transactions (regardless of gas price) be sorted by this system, then it opens the system up to attack vectors where people spam it with low gas price transactions that aren't actually likely to be included. Good suggestion. Will do so shortly in Flashbots Discord. Meanwhile will hold a MEV Roast end of this month on re-orgs. You could improve network efficiency (fewer msgs) and solve that by having fewer validators securing the content layer and publishing their chunks to the structural layer only validators flashbots discord isn't credibly neutral then need channel in this discord The eip1559 base fee prevents this Youve shown you are willing to change the base layer <@301186049323958275>, I've seen the block proposer idea. Formalising MEVA in the base layer will be a disaster because it maximizes MEV, including but not limited to effects such as L2 rollup/fraud proof censorship My proposal is a credible alternative to first reduce and finally eradicate MEV With a bit of extra work censorship can be avoided. For example you could have the proposer list transactions which must be included, and the builders would need to add them to their block It gives you one more shot. Plain Alex gives you perhaps 6 more per block. Dark/Fair upgrades fix it completely My recommendation is to put together a complete proposal that lays everything out. Then iterate on that to pair it down to the most simple solution possible. The problem is that I have seen dozens of "solving MEV" proposals and they all are flawed (usually in a pretty common set of ways). This, unfortunately, makes it hard to get eyes on new proposals because it becomes an increasing time sink to look at and debunk every proposal that comes through. *Maybe* you have some clever solution that no one has thought of before (despite lots of people thinking about it) but convincing people of that is a really hard problem due to the low signal to noise ratio on this particular topic. The more you can do do simplify your solution in as few words as possible (without leaving big open questions) the better. I recognize this is not ideal, but it is the reality of the world we live in unfortunately. As an example, I pretty much ignore all "MEV Solution" proposals now because it has become just too much of a time sink to bother reading them (I'm not even bothering to debunk them anymore). Yeah I get it, and I will be. Only having a doc for the random version is not helping the cause Something that helps encourage me personally to evaluate a proposal is seeing that the author really *gets* the underlying problem up front. Many authors of such proposals seem to fail to fully grok the situation which is what leads them to insufficient solutions. If I see a proposal that makes it very clear that the author groks the problem at a very fundamental level I am more likely to read further than if an author makes some high level claims that suggests they may not fully grok the problem. I can't say how exactly to express this deep intuitive understanding of the problem in an introduction paragraph, but it is one of those things where in the past I "know it when I see it". Maybe opening with the fact that I discovered MEV in 2014 might help 😅 But yeah- good idea. That's helpful thanks "MEV" has been around since basically the dawn of finance, so 2014 is pretty recent. 😉 No it hasn't! Its presentation has changed over time as technology has changed, but the core of it has always been there. It is an information and speed asymmetry problem. If I have information about what you are going to do in the future, I can exploit that knowledge to take some action. For example, if I know that you have a caravan full of silks from across the country on the way to a city before the silks arrive, I can offload all of my silks onto the market before you get there. No other market in history has allowed visibility of 100000s of txs and a lone actor to pick and reorder 100s of them at once! Inversely, if I know you have a representative on the way to the city to buy a large amount of silks, I can buy up all the silks in town before you get there. Technology has only changed the speed and volume at which this sort of information asymmetry can be exploited. It hasn't created a new class of information asymmetry. The same is true for arbitrage (you buy all the silk from city A, I quickly go buy silk from city B and bring it back to city A and sell it at a profit). Rationalizations Micah. Ethereum is worse at markets than centralized regulated competitors. When I explain the situation to my mates in finance they either literally drop their jaws or lol. If the core devs cannot appreciate the severity of this problem then Ethereum is ngmi Centralized markets just create privileged actors who have the capability

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Centralized markets just create privileged actors who have the capability to exploit certain classes of information while everyone else doesn't.  They then utilize external systems (threat of violence via legal system for example) to try to disincentivize those privileged actors from exploiting their power.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Which sometimes works, sometimes doesn't.  At the least, it creates an avenue for corruption that can (and is in some countries) heavily exploited by politicians and regulators for personal gain.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: This circles back to the ethos of Ethereum and crypto-currencies in general, which is to remove privileged roles from the system.  Everyone has equal rights and any specific roles/responsibilities that a particular actor has has as low as possible of a barrier to entry so anyone can take up that role.

excerpts.author: pmcgoohan

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Maintaining this ethos often means we have to make decisions that cause us to do a worse than a centralized solution along some axis.  A perfect example of this is speed.  A centralized platform can execute transactions in milliseconds, while it takes us many seconds to do the same thing.  This is the price we pay for removing privileged actors from the system.

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content:
I agree that removing privileged actors is the current ethos, ... But Im not sure it should be that way, with having most priority. 

Imo highest priority is removing tail risk. Trusted relationships are only bad imo because if they break down there's adverse consequences. But probability of breakdown is usually low. Crypto provides more transparencies into the modes of breakdown, which in turn can be used to design better and remove these in the first place. Transparency also promotes knowing what the breakdown modes and likelihoods of occuring are in the first place, even if they cannot be removed. This is more beneficial than say a judicial system (how much does it cost to DDOS a court with meaningless cases? How far do social incentives need to be engineered to bribe a court? Nobody knows)


If you can clearly define who the trusted actors are and what degree of trust you're placing, you also have the side benefit of sometimes being able to make it non-privileged (for instance once you realise incentives and trust for a single block producer you can rotate it using PoW or PoS). But idk if this is a the primary goal.

excerpts.content: These aren't privileged actors, they are incentivized actors.  Anyone can take on that role without anyone else's permission.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: A privileged actor is someone who has permission/access/responsibilities that someone else cannot take on should they wish to due to some artificial constraint.

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Broadly that's true for any system. Anyone can become a judge. Anyone can become a politician. Question then is barrier for entry, trustworthiness / trustlessness once they get the position, incentives, etc

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Can't run performant systems without privileged actors imo ... You can only reduce the degree of trust and control you place in such actors

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: You cannot anonymously become a judge, and you cannot become a politician without people approving you to become one.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Which is exactly why Ethereum is not a performant system.  🙂

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Yup but I'd want to build or see built .. performant systems on ethereum or using similar tech :)

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Can be more  ambitious

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If you are willing to accept privileged actors you can do way better than a traditional blockchain.

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Anything significantly better than status quo is worth building, doesn't have to eliminate privileged actors altogether

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I think the reason people like Binance copy Ethereum is mainly for marketing and laziness.  You could do significantly better by just having a publicly readable journaling database with signed transactions.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: All the performance of traditional internet systems, with all of the transparency of a blockchain.

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Who runs the database?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The privileged actor of your choice.  🙂

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If all you want from a blockchain is transparency, this is a great solution.

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Yup, so I want to remove unfounded trust and control .. not privilege

excerpts.author: ghosts_in_the_code
excerpts.content: Centralised dB doesn't do that

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: A while back I came up with a Proof of Benevolence idea for sorting.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Essentially the system was centrally sorted (centralized DB more or less), but individual users ran copies of the DB.  If at any point the centralized sorter did anything untoward the client would disconnect from them.  It even had a mechanism for dealing with censorship.
